sections.overview: Plesiothele fentoni is a little-known trapdoor spider endemic to Tasmania, Australia.
sections.identification: It grows to about 1.5 cm and has a yellow-brown abdomen with a distinctive chevron pattern.
sections.habitat: It is recorded from subalpine woodland at Lake Fenton and, tentatively, tall wet forest near Tarraleah.
sections.diet: Its diet is not described in the available species account.
sections.behavior: It lives in a silk-lined, lidless burrow about 5 cm deep, usually among soft moss.
sections.reproduction: The reviewed account provides no detailed information on its breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: The known sites are few, and damage to mossy burrow habitat from trampling is a documented concern.
sections.conservation: Tasmania lists the species as Endangered; the state account also identifies possible development and infrastructure works as threats.
